# **October 22, 2026 — Project Research, Content Development and Team Meeting**

### **\`Activity and Purpose**

Today, I continued researching and developing content for our team project, *Algorithms, Data Structures and Connectionist AI*. I focused on Chapter 2, **Essential Python for the Guide**, and Chapter 3, **Measuring Algorithm Efficiency**. My main purpose was to understand the concepts and prepare well-organized learning materials for the project. I also attended a team meeting to discuss our project progress.

### **My Contribution**

I worked on improving the project outline and organizing the topics into a logical learning sequence. For Chapter 2, I explored Python fundamentals, including variables, operators, conditional statements, loops, functions, lists, and debugging.

For Chapter 3, I researched algorithm efficiency, including time complexity, Big-O notation, common growth rates, nested loops, and space complexity. I also used ChatGPT to help develop structured educational content and examples for these chapters.

### **Outcome and Evidence**

I prepared a more detailed chapter outline and obtained AI-assisted draft learning materials, including a Chapter 2 document with Python examples. The Chapter 3 outline was also organized into ten sections.

**Evidence:** Screenshots of my October 22  Google research conversations, and the meeting footage.

### **Learning and Reflection**

While researching, I realized that understanding Python syntax alone is not enough for studying algorithms. It is also important to understand how algorithms operate and how their efficiency changes with input size.

Some concepts, especially time complexity and Big-O notation, were difficult for me initially. Breaking them into smaller topics helped me understand what I need to study further. I also recognized the importance of checking AI-generated explanations before using them in our final project.

# **October 23, 2026 — Project Research, Content Outline Development and Team Work**

**Activity and purpose**

Today, I attended a team meeting and worked on the content outline for our project. The purpose was to organize a beginner-friendly learning path and keep the study guide, PowerPoint presentation, and videos achievable within one month.

**My contribution**

I prepared the content outline and organized its main chapters and subtopics. The outline became too comprehensive, so I revised it following laoshi’s feedback. I kept the main topic structure while reducing subchapters, technical details, and extra content, aiming to retain about one-third of the original scope. I also worked on the outline’s format and presentation and updated my personal learning log to record today’s teamwork and individual contribution.

**Outcome**

I produced a smaller, more focused outline for the project. The revised direction prioritizes essential concepts and simple examples that can interest beginners and help them explore further. It gives our team a more manageable basis for developing the three deliverables within the available month.

**Learning and reflection**

I learned that including more information does not automatically make a study guide stronger. My first outline covered too much for our audience and deadline. Laoshi’s feedback helped me understand that quality depends on selecting useful content and explaining it clearly. I also learned to consider the workload across all three deliverables, while allowing time for checking and revision. Team discussion helped me connect my content work with the overall project plan.

**AI use — ChatGPT**

I used ChatGPT to help review and shorten the outline according to the teacher’s feedback, organize its wording and format, and draft today’s personal log. I supplied the project context and constraints. The AI-assisted outline and log still need my final review for accuracy and consistency with the team’s agreed scope.
